chain.label: King Air pilot likely below peak alertness (early wake-up, end of long flying day, 1701 accident time)
chain.trigger: Based on his early wake-up time, the time of day that the accident occurred, and the possibility that he had difficulty sleeping recently, he was most likely not at his peak alertness at the time of the accident.

chain.label: King Air pilot and pilot-rated passenger preoccupied with in-cockpit instruction, each relying on the other
chain.trigger: suggesting that they may have been preoccupied with instructional activities inside the cockpit

chain.label: No staffed on-airport ARFF at Quincy; not required under Part 139 for the 19-seat operation, city fire department 10 miles away
chain.trigger: The truck at the airport was not staffed at the time of the accident because no air carrier aircraft with more than 30 passenger seats were landing or taking off.

chain.label: Beech 1900C air stair door exterior release required depressing an unoutlined black button, marked only by a small low-contrast placard
chain.trigger: The FBO pilot said that he did not know that the proper procedure for opening the door involved depressing the button above the handle while simultaneously turning the handle.

chain.label: King Air occupants failed to monitor the CTAF and failed to scan for traffic, never detecting the landing Beech 1900C
chain.trigger: the failure of the pilots in the King Air A90 to effectively monitor the common traffic advisory frequency or to properly scan for traffic

caused_by.evidence: he was most likely not at his peak alertness at the time of the accident

A combination of these factors (preoccupation with providing instruction to the pilot/passenger, careless habits, possible fatigue, and rushing) could explain why the King Air pilot did not properly scan for traffic.

chain.label: King Air pilot began the takeoff roll without announcing takeoff intentions on the CTAF
chain.trigger: Although he had been sitting on runway 04 for about 1 minute, the King Air pilot began the takeoff without making a takeoff announcement over the CTAF.

caused_by.evidence: they may have been preoccupied with instructional activities inside the cockpit

chain.label: Inexperienced Cherokee pilot answered flight 5925's query that was directed at the King Air; his reply was clipped by the 1900C GPWS callout
chain.trigger: at 1700:28, the pilot of the Cherokee stated, 'seven six four six Juliet...holding...for departure on runway four.' The CVR then recorded an interruption in this transmission by a mechanical 'two hundred' alert announcement

chain.label: Flight 5925 crew misinterpreted the reply as the King Air agreeing to hold, and stopped being concerned about it
chain.trigger: they mistook the Cherokee pilot's transmission (that he was holding for departure on runway 4) as a response from the King Air to their request for the King Air's intentions

caused_by.evidence: the Cherokee pilot's interrupted radio transmission, which led to the Beech 1900C pilot's misunderstanding of the transmission as an indication from the King Air that it would not take off until after flight 5925 had cleared the runway

chain.label: King Air commenced its takeoff roll on runway 04 while flight 5925 was landing on intersecting runway 13
chain.trigger: resulting in their commencing a takeoff roll when the Beech 1900C (United Express flight 5925) was landing on an intersecting runway

caused_by.evidence: the occupants of the King Air must have been unaware at the time they began their takeoff roll that an airplane was about to land

chain.label: The two airplanes collided at the intersection of runways 13 and 04
chain.trigger: At 1701, during flight 5925's landing rollout, the airplane collided with the King Air at the intersection of runways 13 and 04.

caused_by.evidence: The King Air's tire scuff marks veered continually to the right on runway 04 for about 260 feet before they converged with the skid marks from the Beech 1900C.

Having received what they believed was an assurance from the airplane on the runway that it was going to hold, the pilots may have become less concerned about continuing to watch the King Air during their landing.
Such an announcement would have afforded the Beech 1900C flightcrew the opportunity to take evasive action.

chain.label: Intense fuel-fed postcrash pool fire engulfed the King Air and the right side of the Beech 1900C, filling the cabin with smoke
chain.trigger: They saw that the King Air and the right side of the Beech 1900C were engulfed in fire.

caused_by.evidence: Both aircraft were destroyed by the impact and postcrash fire.

chain.label: Air stair door was not opened by the occupants or by the two would-be rescuers, and the left overwing hatch was never opened
chain.trigger: the failure of the air stair door on the Beech 1900C to be opened

caused_by.evidence: The FBO pilot said that he did not know that the proper procedure for opening the door involved depressing the button above the handle while simultaneously turning the handle.

chain.label: All 14 occupants of the two airplanes died of smoke inhalation despite survivable impact forces
chain.trigger: the cause of death for 10 occupants was 'carbon monoxide intoxication from inhalation of smoke and soot.' The cause of death for four occupants was 'inhalation of products of combustion.'

caused_by.evidence: The bodies of the King Air's occupants were found behind the seats in the cockpit, indicating that they were overcome by the effects of the fire before reaching an exit.
the occupants of the Beech 1900C did not escape because the air stair door and the left overwing exit hatch were not opened for undetermined reasons
If on-airport aircraft rescue and firefighting equipment protection had been required for this operation at Quincy Airport, lives might have been saved.
